examples.solution_text:
(a) No vertex or edge repeats. This is a path, a trail and a walk.

(b) The edges $KJ$, $JM$, $MN$ and $NJ$ are distinct, but $J$ repeats. This is a trail and a walk, but not a path. It is not closed.

(c) The route returns to $J$, with no repeated edge and no other repeated vertex. It is a cycle, a circuit, a trail and a walk.

(d) Every edge is used exactly once and the route returns to $J$. It is an Eulerian circuit, so it is also a circuit, an Eulerian trail, a trail and a walk. It is not a cycle because $J$ is revisited partway through.

(e) $KJ$ and $JK$ are the same undirected edge. The edge repeats, so this is a walk but not a trail, path, circuit or cycle.

examples.question_text: A network has $9$ edges. Explain why it cannot have exactly three vertices of odd degree.
examples.solution_text:
Each edge contributes two ends to the degree total, including a loop whose two ends meet the same vertex.

$\text{Sum of degrees}=2\times9=18$.

The even degrees add to an even number. Three odd degrees add to an odd number, so together they would give an odd total, contradicting $18$.

The number of odd-degree vertices must be even.
